# AzureContainerAppTarget

<!-- GENERATED by tools/gen_component_agents.py from xrds/azurecontainerapptarget.meta.yaml; edit the sidecar, not this file. -->

The minimum Azure infrastructure a container deploys into on Container Apps - a resource group, a Container Apps environment and the app with public ingress, seeded with a placeholder image. Disposable: delete the XR to remove all of it.

## How it is requested

A stand-alone XR request in the tenants repo (`tenants/<app>/xr-requests/`), or composed by a function app with `spec.target.enabled`. See docs/user/cloud-targets.md.

## Conditions

Besides Crossplane's Ready and Synced. Reasons are a closed set:

- `TargetReady`: `AzureContainerAppTargetReady` (True), `AzureContainerAppTargetProvisioning` (False).

## Verify a live XR

```
tools/airframe-verify azurecontainerapptarget <namespace>/<name> [--context CTX]
```

Read-only. Steps, after the implicit `xr-synced` check:

- `xr-ready` (condition): The AzureContainerAppTarget XR's TargetReady condition has reason AzureContainerAppTargetReady.
- `app-running` (cloudCli): az containerapp show --name {appName} --resource-group {resourceGroup} reports properties.runningStatus Running.
- `url-answers` (http): An HTTP GET of status.url returns a response (the Azure Functions placeholder serves its landing page).

## Editing this composition

- Edit `compositions/azurecontainerapptarget/templates/`, never the inline blocks in `composition.yaml`: `python3 tools/build-compositions azurecontainerapptarget` splices them.
- `python3 tools/test_compositions.py --update azurecontainerapptarget` regenerates `example/expected/`; review that diff like code, it is the behaviour change.
- `python3 tools/test_sidecars.py` fails if a template change breaks a name this sidecar promises.
- Azure forbids '/' in tag names: tags here are hangar-target / hangar-component / hangar-app, not the hangar.io/* labels used on Kubernetes and AWS.

Contract: `tools/airframe-capabilities verify azurecontainerapptarget`; schema: `xrds/azurecontainerapptarget.yaml`.
